record.title: C7 — Theorem C7 (the ℓ^{2/3} term of the elder density), with Theorem E, Corollary E1 and Proposition G₀

statements.text:
- **Theorem C7 (the `ℓ^{2/3}` term of the elder density)** (§5). In every `d ≥ 2` and for every `L`, as `ℓ ↓ 0`,

      ν_eld(ℓ) = c ℓ^{−1/3} + c₁ ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ ℓ^{1/3} + (c₃ − R_{2/3}) ℓ^{2/3} + ν_eld^{far,r_0^*}(ℓ) + o(ℓ^{2/3}),         (C7.1)
      ρ_rej(ℓ) + ν_eld^{far,r_0^*}(ℓ) = B_{d,L} + (I^{cand} − c₁) ℓ^{1/4} + R_{2/3} ℓ^{2/3} + o(ℓ^{2/3}),                (C7.2)

**Theorem E (the elder weight on `κ ≤ r`).** There are `r_* > 0` and `C, N` such that for `0 < r ≤ r_*`, `b ∈ R`,
`u ∈ S^{d−1}` and `0 < k ≤ r²`,

    E_Q[(W_r/r²) e] ≤ C r² [ Υ(r, κ) + r²κ^{2/3} ] P^N,        0 ≤ 𝐓_r^{eld}(k, u) ≤ C [ Υ(r, κ) + r²κ^{2/3} ].         (E)

Moreover, with the same `r_*`, `C` and `N` (in particular `C` does not depend on `ε`), for `0 < ε ≤ 1` the part of the
good region where `μ < ε` satisfies

    E_Q[(W_r/r²) e 1_{𝒢∩{μ<ε}}] ≤ C r² [ εrκ + r^{7/3}κ^{2/3}log(2/r) ] P^N,                                           (E′)

so the corresponding part of `𝐓_r^{eld}(k, u)` is at most `C[εrκ + r^{7/3}κ^{2/3}log(2/r)]`, uniformly in `u`.

**Corollary E1 (the remainders without the logarithm).** As `ℓ ↓ 0`, `∫_{ℓ^{1/5}}^{r_0^*}∫𝐓_r^{eld}(ℓ/r³, u)dσ(u)dr = O(ℓ^{2/3})`,
and

    ν_eld(ℓ) = cℓ^{−1/3} + c₁ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ℓ^{1/3} + O(ℓ^{2/3}),        ρ_rej(ℓ) = B_{d,L} + (I^{cand} − c₁)ℓ^{1/4} + O(ℓ^{2/3}).   (E1)

**Lemma D (the ridge dichotomy).** Deterministic. In [N] §1's setting (`0 < r ≤ r_Q`, `𝒩 ≥ max(1, ‖f‖_{C⁵})`, and
`A ≤ −λI` with `λ > 0`), let `f ∈ C⁵(X)` have the pins, let `κ > 0`, and assume (Q′1)–(Q′2) and `H̃ < 0`. Assume moreover

    (G)  no point of Φ(𝒲′) other than S is a critical point of f with value f(S).

If `e(f) = 1`, then `g_𝔉(X) ∈ [−κ, 0]` for every `X ∈ [−½, ½]`, or `g_𝔉(X) ∈ [−κ, 0]` for every `X ∈ [−3, −½]`. (G) is
needed by the argument: a ridge with a local minimum of value `−κ` in `(−½, ½)` can defeat both escape and trap and both
alternatives (control K4's tie witness, and mutant M8).

**Lemma D′ ((G) is generic).** For `0 < r ≤ r_0^*`, `b ∈ R`, `u ∈ S^{d−1}` and `0 < k ≤ 1`, `Q`-almost surely no point of `X`
other than `S` is a critical point of `f` with value `f(S)`. In particular (G) holds `Q`-almost surely on `{A < 0}`, where
`𝒲′` is defined.

**Proposition G₀ (the elder kernel at gaps of order `r³`).** For every `c > 0`,
`lim_{r↓0} r^{−3} sup_{u∈S^{d−1}} 𝐓_r^{eld}(cr³, u) = 0`.

**Theorem C7 (the `ℓ^{2/3}` term of the elder density).** In every `d ≥ 2` and for every `L`, (C7.1) and (C7.2) hold as
`ℓ ↓ 0`, with `c₃` of note C3 ((C3)) and `R_{2/3}` of note SL ((SL)); the proof uses #188's Theorem G at a fixed separation
`ρ₀ ≤ r_*` (§5). By #188's Theorem G at `ρ = r_0^*`, `ν_eld^{far,r_0^*}(ℓ) = O(ℓ^N)` for every `N`, so

    ν_eld(ℓ) = cℓ^{−1/3} + c₁ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ℓ^{1/3} + (c₃ − R_{2/3})ℓ^{2/3} + o(ℓ^{2/3}),
    ρ_rej(ℓ) = B_{d,L} + (I^{cand} − c₁)ℓ^{1/4} + R_{2/3}ℓ^{2/3} + o(ℓ^{2/3}).                                         (C7.3)

record.title: higher_configuration — fixed-p compact factorial and Laplace convergence (4)-(5) of the Gaussian candidate process, via the covariance floor (6)

statements.text:
Let `J_infty,u=(F,F_u,F_uu,F_uuu,F_v,F_uv,F_vv)` have the Euclidean covariance `exp(-|h|^2/2)`, and let `p_Jinfty,u` denote its seven-dimensional density. The proposed intensity is

```text
nu(ds db dk dA dy d sigma(u))
 = v_* 144 s^(-1/3) k^(4/3) A^2
       p_Jinfty,u(b,0,0,12k,0,0,A)
           ds db dk dA dy d sigma(u),       A<0.             (3)

Here dy is unit-volume Haar measure and `d sigma` is unnormalized circle arclength, of mass `2pi`. There is no extra `1/2`. The measure is Radon on E and strictly positive on every nonempty open mark box. The claim to be justified conventionally below is, for each **fixed** integer p and `f_i in C_c(E)`,

```text
E integral product_i f_i(z_i) Xi_t^[p](d(z_1,...,z_p))
                  -> product_i integral f_i d nu,           (4)
E exp(-Xi_t(f)) -> exp[-integral(1-exp(-f))d nu],
                  f in C_c(E), f>=0.                        (5)
```

This is the new analytic lemma. For p distinct points `x_i in R^2`, assume `|x_i-x_j|>=eta`, `0<eta<=1`. Let Sigma_raw be the covariance of all `10p` raw derivatives `D^beta F(x_i)`, `|beta|<=3`, for `R(h)=exp(-|h|^2/2)`. Then

`Sigma_raw >= c_p eta^(8p-2) I`, with `c_p>0` depending only on p.       (6)

`Gamma_p,t >= m_p(t) I`, `m_p(t)=c''_p eta^(nu_p)`.        (14)

This is uniform over **all** configurations with minimum torus separation eta and all p frames. It does not compare a fixed nonzero cross-block error to a vanishing floor: (13) is explicitly o of that floor. If all separations exceed R_t, every component is a singleton and the floor improves to a constant `m0/2` for small t. These statements hold for each fixed p; no floor uniform in p is claimed.

To apply the latter Euclidean statement literally, embed E properly as the closed subset `R^4 x (S^1)^3` of `R^10`, using `(log s,b,log k,log(-A))` and the two unit-torus circle coordinates and the u circle. Restrict any `C_c^+(R^10)` test to this closed copy; it is a compact test on E, so (5) applies. The intensity (3), pushed forward and set to zero off this copy, is Radon. The criterion therefore yields the corresponding vague point-process convergence for this **candidate** sector. This last sentence is an application of the named classical criterion; the quantitative work is (4)-(5). It is still a pending-review author conclusion, not project scientific acceptance or source admission.

record.title: reverse_full_projected_ppp — reverse localization (33)-(34) and full lifetime/spatial Poisson Laplace law (36)-(38) in one Gaussian family

statements.text:
For each S>0 and any positive epsilon,a,tau with epsilon,a,tau<=1, and finite A,H,U,R, Section 6 produces a compact K in E containing every actual bar with `epsilon<=ell/t<=S` whose birth conditions (25) hold, for all sufficiently small t. Combining (18)–(24) gives

```text
limsup_(t->0) E[ number of bars with 0<ell/t<=S
                                whose marked atom is outside K ]
 <= C_S [ epsilon^(2/3)+a^3+tau+h(A,H,U)+R^(-8/3) ].  (33)
```

```text
P(every finite bar with 0<ell<=St has its unique
  actual elder saddle in a shrinking local fold chart) ->1,
max_(0<ell<=St) dist_T(M,S) ->0 in probability,         (34)
```

```text
E exp(-Z_t(f))
 -> exp[-v_* c_G integral_(T_1^2) integral_0^infinity
                  (1-exp(-f(s,y))) s^(-1/3) ds dy],   (36)
```

where

```text
c_G=144 integral_(S^1) integral_R integral_(k>0) integral_(A<0)
       k^(4/3) A^2 p_Jinfty,u(b,0,0,12k,0,0,A)
                      dA dk db d sigma(u) >0.          (37)
```

Equation (36) is the full lifetime/spatial Poisson Laplace law, including tests touching zero. The intensity is locally finite on `[0,infinity)xT^2` and has no atom at zero. The same proper closed embedding/Laplace criterion already explicitly imported and reviewed in the accepted higher proof applies to this simpler space: use `[0,infinity)x(S^1)^2` as a closed subset of R5. Thus it also supplies vague convergence in distribution of the projected point processes. This uses the previously named bounded-Laplace convergence import; no expectation convergence for arbitrary unbounded functionals is asserted.

For expected counts, compact first-moment convergence from the same accepted theorem and (33) give, by upper/lower cutoff approximation and the finite continuous limiting density,

```text
E N_bar((0,St]) -> (3/2) v_* c_G S^(2/3),
E N_bar((0,St]) / (Vt^(2/3)) -> (3/2)c_G S^(2/3).      (38)
```

In particular `N_bar((0,St])` converges in distribution to a Poisson variable of mean `(3/2)v_*c_G S^(2/3)`. This also follows from (36) by approximating the cap boundary, whose limiting intensity is zero. The process law retains joint spatial/lifetime structure, not only a one-dimensional count.

This proposed result closes the **probabilistic all-short-bar reverse complement and lifetime/spatial process law for the one declared ideal Gaussian truncation family**, conditional only on the exact accepted conventional inputs and named classical area/Laplace imports. It is stronger than another certificate equivalent to localization: the sufficient birth-jet sectors have a derived vanishing complement, and the saddle is actually constructed.

statements.text:
- **Corollary CJ2 (note C7's coefficient).** At #244 Theorem A's conditional scope, `J/30 − Ĩ ≥ 0.311509`, so for every real
  `L ≥ 10`: `(c₃ − R_{2/3})(L) ≥ 0.035768` (`d = 3`; `≥ 0.035825` for `L ≥ 24`) and `≥ 0.028472` (`d = 2`). Note DC had
  `0.1711𝒮_d`, that is `0.019677` and `0.015639`. The exploration values are `0.0774672` and `0.0615684` (note V24,
  Remark 1); the certified bounds are about 46% of them. The bound is one-sided because `D` has no certified lower bound.

**Proposition 2.** On the partition of `[10⁻⁶, 30]` into 1500 cells,
- `300` geometric cells on `[10⁻⁶, 0.05]` (ratio `(5·10⁴)^{1/300}`),
- uniform cells: `400` on `[0.05, 1]`, `300` on `[1, 4]`, `300` on `[4, 12]` and `200` on `[12, 30]`,

every interior point rounded to 12 significant digits (which changes only the geometric piece and `[4, 12]`, whose step `2/75`
is not a terminating decimal), the sum of the Simpson values of `hψ` with the remainders (3.1), Lemma 4 with `A₀ = 10⁻⁶` and

record.title: A4_1 — Theorem QFE′_K (A4's planar rate uniform over a compact gap interval K, every β < 2/3), with Lemma LE_K and Corollary SE_K

statements.text:
**Lemma LE_K.** Let `f` be `C⁴` with the exact pins at a gap `k ∈ K`, with `y ∈ Rsec`. Suppose `Rch ≤ w`, `w ≥ 1` and `r(1 + k_+)w ≤ L/4`.
- **(i)** For every `ξ ∈ K_raw`, `|E_r(ξ)| ≤ K₂(K) N r w²·|ξ − raw M|² ≤ 4K₂(K) N r w²·|v|²`.
- **(ii)** `4h ≥ 2ℓ_M|v|²`, where `ℓ_M := min(1, a_M/(γ² + 72))`. (A4 calls this margin `ℓ`.)
- **Consequently**, if `η_K N < ℓ_M`, then `F_r(raw M + 2v) > 0`.

**Corollary LE_K (the rejected certificate at gap `k`).** For `w ≥ 1` with `r(1 + k_+)w ≤ L/4`, put on `Rsec`

    Good_LE,K(r, w) := {Rch ≤ w,  E0(r, w) < μ/2,  η_K N(γ² + 72) < a_M,  η_K N < 1}.

This event is measurable, and on it `D_f(M_r) > f(S_r)`.

**Lemma B′_K (the endpoint strip at gap `k`).** Assume also `η_K ≤ 1`. Then

    μ_r(D_Λ ∩ Rsec ∩ {η_K N(γ² + 72) ≥ a_M  or  η_K N ≥ 1}) ≤ C_K[H³η_K + rH⁴√η_K].

**Lemma Band_K (the decision band at general `p`).** Assume also `w ≥ 5` and `r(1 + k_+)w ≤ L/4`. For `0 < d ≤ 1/4` and every fixed real `p ≥ 1`,

    μ_r(D_Λ ∩ (E ∪ Rsec) ∩ {E0 ≥ |μ|/2}) ≤ C_{K,p}[d + rH⁴ + H³(e/d)^p],    e = rw⁴.

**Theorem QFE′_K.** Work in C103's setting. For each fixed `β ∈ (0, 2/3)` there are `C_{K,β} < ∞` and `r_{K,β} > 0`, uniform over `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ K` and all frames, such that for `r ≤ r_{K,β}`

    ‖ν_r^F − ν_0^F‖_var ≤ C_{K,β} r^β,    1 − p_r = r³(α₁ + α₂) + O_{K,β}(r^{3+β}).

Here `α_j` are CUB's G11 coefficients at gap `k` (C103 (S34)). The conditional raw-jet law given `F_r` converges at the same rate.

**Corollary SE_K.** Fix `Λ ≥ 1` and `ε ∈ (0, 2/3)`. Set `w = r^{−1/12}` and `d = r^{2/3−ε}`, and fix a real `p ≥ 2/(3ε)`. Uniformly over `b`, `k ∈ K` and frames, for all sufficiently small `r`,

    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ (E ∪ Rsec) ∩ (H_r Δ E)) ≤ C_{K,Λ,ε} r^{11/3−ε}.

In particular, `Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ Rsec ∩ H_r)` and `Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ E \ H_r)` are both `O(r^{11/3−ε})`.

statements.text:
**Theorem C127, conditional on the retained interfaces in §2.**
For each fixed R>=4 and integer p>=0 there are finite C_(R,p),r_(R,p)>0,
uniform in b in B and all frames, such that for 0<r<=r_(R,p) and
rho=r^(1/100),

    E_(Q_r^W)[N^p N_R N_far^rho] <= C_(R,p)r^(427/100).    (3)

In particular it is O_(R,p)(r^4). In the original pinned law,

    E_(Q_r)[W_r N^p N_R N_far^rho]
                     <= C_(R,p)r^(627/100)=O_(R,p)(r^6).  (4)

record.title: A3 — Lemma SR and Theorems QS-E′_d, QS-R_d: the trap window in every d ≥ 3 under explicit hard-barrel conditions

statements.text:
Assume (B1) and (B2). Then for every `x ∈ Ω` the following hold.
- **(a)** `g(x, ·)` has a unique maximizer `ζ(x)` on `B̄_ε`. It lies in the interior, satisfies `|ζ(x)| ≤ q₀(x)/Λ < ε/2`, and is the only critical point of `g(x, ·)` in `B_ε`.
- **(b)** The reduced height `G(x) := g(x, ζ(x))` satisfies `0 ≤ G(x) − g(x, 0) ≤ q₀(x)²/(2Λ)`.
- **(c)** `g(x, z) ≤ G(x) − (Λ/2)|z − ζ(x)|²` for `|z| ≤ ε` ([HFL] §7 with `A = ΛI`). On `|z| = ε` the inequality `g(x, z) < G(x) − Λε²/8` is strict.
- **(d)** `ζ ∈ C¹(Ω)` and `G ∈ C²(Ω)`. Moreover `∇G = g_x` and `D²G = g_xx − g_xz g_zz⁻¹ g_zx`, both evaluated at `(x, ζ(x))` ([HFL] (SC)). Hence

      ‖D²G(x) − D²_x g(x, 0)‖ ≤ N₃ q₀(x)/Λ + N_xz²/Λ.

- **(e)** If a pin lies in `Ω`, then `ζ = 0` there, and `G` inherits the pin. So `G(M) = 0`, `G(S) = −1`, and `∇G(M) = ∇G(S) = 0` for pins in `Ω`.

**Hypotheses.**
- `ψ > |c|`, with any `R`, `Δ` included.
- **(H)** for `P`, with `η`.
- (B1)–(B3) on `Ω × B̄_ε`, with `Ω ⊃ 𝔚_E`.
- Exact pins in `ℝ^d`.
- With `e_G := G − P`:
  - **(E1_d)** `|e_G| < η` on `𝔚_E` (it suffices on `V′_η`);
  - **(E2_d)** `‖J_S D²e_G J_S‖ ≤ 2/5` on `E_S`;
  - **(E3_d)** `‖J_M D²e_G J_M‖ < 1` on `E_M`.

**Conclusion.** `d_g(M̂) = −1 = g(Ŝ)`.

**Hypotheses.**
- `ψ > |c|`, `0 < μ < 1`, and `Y` is the highest extra saddle of `P`.
- `K := {M + t(Y − M) : 0 ≤ t ≤ 2} ⊂ 𝔚_R`.
- (B1)–(B2) on `Ω × B̄_ε`, with `Ω ⊃ K`. (B3) is not needed.
- `g(M̂) = 0` and `g_z(M̂) = 0`.
- `|e_G| < min(μ, 4(1 − μ))` on `K`. It suffices that `|e₀| + q₀²/(2Λ) < min(μ, 4(1 − μ))` there.

**Conclusion.** `d_g(M̂) > −1`. With the value pin `g(Ŝ) = −1`, this is rejection: `d_g(M̂) > g(Ŝ)`.

record.title: A3_3 — Proposition W3 (the d = 3 soft-layer weight with O(r) error, uniform as λ₂ → 0), Lemma P and Corollary TE

statements.text:
**Lemma P (the pin Hessians).** There is `C = C(k_±)` such that for `0 < r ≤ 1` and both pins,

    Hess 𝔉(p) = diag(P_p, −λ₂/k) + r^{1/2} [[0, Da(p)], [Da(p)ᵀ, 0]] + E_p,    ‖E_p‖ ≤ CNr,                         (P.1)

with the model blocks of #243 (Step 3 of Theorem FL's proof)

    P_{M̂₀} = [[−6, −γ/2], [−γ/2, −λ̃ − kB/2]],    P_{Ŝ₀} = [[6, γ/2], [γ/2, −λ̃ + kB/2]],
    det P_{M̂₀} = 6λ̃ + Y,    det P_{Ŝ₀} = −6λ̃ + Y,    Da(p) = (±γ₂/(2k), ±β₂/2)   (sign of the pin's X).

Put `w := (6λ̃ + Y)₊(6λ̃ − Y)₊` and `Π := 1 + |λ̃| + γ² + |B| + N`.

**Proposition W3.** There is `C = C(k_±)` such that for `0 < r ≤ 1` with `rN ≤ 1`,

    |W_r/r⁴ − (λ₂)₊² w| ≤ C rN (|λ₂| + rN) Π⁴ (1 + |λ₂|)².                                                     (W3)

- The bound holds for every sign and size of `λ̃` and `λ₂`, with no lower bound on `λ₂`. The pins may be typed or untyped.

**Corollary TE (typing edges).** Assume `rN ≤ 1`, and let `ε_r` be the right side of (W3). Call the model untyped when `(λ₂)₊²w = 0`. Then:
- `(λ₂)₊²w > ε_r` implies `W_r > 0`, so both pins are typed;
- `W_r > 0` with the model untyped implies `W_r/r⁴ ≤ ε_r`.

So, for any law of pinned fields, `E[(W_r/r⁴)1{model untyped, rN ≤ 1}] ≤ E[ε_r1{rN ≤ 1}]`.

record.title: A3_6 — Theorems E₃, R₃ and BL₃: the d = 3 weighted decision on the bounded soft layer, with Lemma SC

statements.text:
1. **Theorem E₃** (§3), C94 in `d = 3`.
   - On the model elder sector `E`, a good event fails with weighted mass `O(r^{7/2})`. It is built from A3.5's barrel, reduced height and Hessian transfer, with C94's random tolerance `τ_E = ½min(v, −μ)`.
   - On the good event, A3's QS-E′_d decides elder pairing.
   - The new estimate is the hard-gap term `C_e kN²rw⁴/λ₂` of A3.5's (D₃) against the random tolerance, through A3.5's joint edge–gap majorant (E₃⁺).
2. **Lemma SC and Theorem R₃** (§4), C97 in `d = 3`. C97's two-margin chord certifies rejection when drawn in the plane of the pin axis and the soft eigenvector. It needs no barrel, no reduced height, no gradient pin and no bound on `λ₂`. This removes the hard gap from the rejected side; the bad mass is again `O(r^{7/2})`.
3. **Theorem BL₃** (§5), C98 in `d = 3`. `Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ (H_r Δ E)) ≤ Cr^{7/2}` and `Q_r^W(H_r | D_Λ) = m_E/m_Λ + O(√r)`, with a joint jet/Boolean total-variation bound. All are uniform in `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ [k₋, k₊]` and the frame.

**Theorem E₃.**
- **(a) The certificate.** On `Good^E`, `D_f(M_r) = f(S_r)`, and `M_r` and `S_r` are nondegenerate with Morse indices 3 and 2. On the Morse locus, `H_r` holds.
- **(b) The bad mass.** For `0 < ϱ ≤ 1/4` and finite `p ≥ 1`,

      Q_r^W(E ∖ Good^E) ≤ C r³[w^{−8} + rw^{−4} + e + r√e + ϱ + r + (e/ϱ)^p + (e/ϱ)⁴ + r(e/ϱ)² + e⁴ + re² + r²w⁴].   (3.2)

- **(c) The rate.** With `w = r^{−1/16}`, `ϱ = r^{1/2}` and `p = 2`, for `r` small,

      Q_r^W(E ∖ Good^E) ≤ C r^{7/2},    Q_r^W(E ∖ H_r) ≤ C r^{7/2}.                                          (3.3)

**Lemma SC.** Let `f ∈ C(X)` with `f(M_r) = b` and `f(S_r) = b − kr³`. Let `(u, e₁, e₂)` be an orthonormal frame with `u` the pin axis, and let `k, r > 0`. Let `γ ≠ 0`, `λ̃`, `B` and `C₃` be real numbers with `ψ > |c|` and `0 < μ < 1`. In the application they are the jets of `f` in its eigenframe. Let `Y*` and `K` be as in §0, and `g` as there. Put `e₀ := g(·, ·, 0) − P_QS` on `𝔚_R`, the error of the planar section. If

    sup_K |e₀| < min(μ, 4h_Y),                                                                              (4.1)

then `D_f(M_r) > f(S_r)`. No gradient pin, no barrel and no bound on `λ₂` is used.

**Theorem R₃** ((a) deterministic, (b)–(c) conditional on A3.4). For `0 < r ≤ r₀` and deterministic `w ≥ 5`, define inside `Rsec`

    Good^R(r, w) := Rsec ∩ {ρ_R < w} ∩ {sup_{Ω̄_w}|ℰ(·, ·, 0)| < τ_R}.                                     (4.2)

It is Borel, for the reasons given after (3.1).

    μ_r(U ∩ {|μ| ≤ δN}) ≤ C(δ + r),                                                                        (2.3)
    μ_r(U ∩ {λ₂|μ| ≤ δN²}) ≤ C(δ + r).                                                                     (2.4)

    Q_r^W(E ∖ Good^E) ≤ C r³[w^{−8} + rw^{−4} + e + r√e + r + e⁴ + re² + r²w⁴].                           (5.1)

With `w = r^{−1/12}`, for `r` small,

    Q_r^W(E ∖ Good^E) ≤ C r^{11/3},    Q_r^W(E ∖ H_r) ≤ C r^{11/3}.                                         (5.2)

**Theorem R₃′ (the rejected side).** For `0 < r ≤ r₀` and deterministic `w ≥ 5` with `η_LE ≤ 1`,

record.title: A3_9 — Theorem 9.2 (A3.8's α^{(3)} = F/(kA_0), and a_fail = a1 + a2 at #175's scope) and Corollary 9.3 (rates in d = 3)

statements.text:
**Theorem 9.2.** For `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ [k₋, k₊]` and every frame `R` with `u = Re_1`,

    α^{(3)}(b, k, R) = F(k; b, u)/(kA_0(b, k, u)),                                                                 (9.2)

where `α^{(3)} = z₀^{−1}∫1_{Rsec^{(∞)}}k^{−1}λ₂³ρ₀(A₀(λ₂, θ), t)w_λdϑ` is A3.8's coefficient and `F` is #242 (3.1)'s fold-scale limit. In particular `α^{(3)}` depends on the frame only through `u`, and `F(k; b, u) = kA_0α^{(3)} ∈ [kA_0M_*, kA_0M^*]` with A3.8 Lemma 5.3's constants. Under #175's stated scope, moreover

    α^{(3)}(b, k, u) = a_fail(b, k, u) = a1 + a2                                                                   (9.3)

(#175 (S2)), so A3.8 is the rate version of the scalar part of #175's (S3) and of #243's (4.1) in `d = 3`.

**Corollary 9.3 (Theorem FL and Corollary FL.5 with a rate).** In `d = 3`, for every fixed `β ∈ (0, 2/3)` there are `C_β` and `r_β > 0`, and there are `C` and `r_* ∈ (0, e^{−1}]`, uniform over `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ [k₋, k₊]` and the frame, such that

statements.text:
- **Theorem V (the transfer)** (§5). Take `d ∈ {2, 3}`, a real `L ≥ 10` and the [P] torus field. Then note C3's coefficient
  `c₃(L)` and note SL's `R_{2/3}(L)` differ from their model values `c₃^∞ = (J/30)𝒮_d` and `R^∞ = Ĩ𝒮_d` by at most the
  following multiples of `𝒮_d := ∫_{S^{d−1}}∫_RF₀ db dσ`, with the model's `F₀` (#242's Corollary 1′):

  | `d` | `c₃`, `L ≥ 10` | `R_{2/3}`, `L ≥ 10` | `c₃`, `L ≥ 24` | `R_{2/3}`, `L ≥ 24` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | `5.88·10⁻⁹` | `7.81·10⁻⁶` | `4.88·10⁻¹¹⁰` | `6.48·10⁻¹⁰⁷` |
  | 3 | `1.97·10⁻⁷` | `4.97·10⁻⁴` | `1.64·10⁻¹⁰⁸` | `4.13·10⁻¹⁰⁵` |

**Lemma K (a global bound for `Φ`).** For all real `t` and `χ₀`,

    |Φ(1 − t, χ₀ + 8 − 12t) − I_quad(t, χ₀)| ≤ 324 (t² + |t|³ + |χ₀| + χ₀²).                                         (K)

**Theorem V (the transfer).** Let `d ∈ {2, 3}` and `L₀ ∈ {10, 24}`. For every real `L ≥ L₀`, `|c₃(L) − c₃^∞| ≤ η_c𝒮_d` and
`|R_{2/3}(L) − R^∞| ≤ η_R𝒮_d`, with `η_c` and `η_R` the entries of the table above for that `L₀`. The `R_{2/3}` bound is at
#244 Theorem A's conditional scope; the `c₃` bound does not use #244.

**Corollary V1.** For `d ∈ {2, 3}` and every real `L ≥ 10`, `c₃(L) ≥ (1/60000 − 1.97·10⁻⁷)𝒮_d > 0`. So the remainder
`O(ℓ^{2/3})` of note LU's Theorem P⁺ is of exact order `ℓ^{2/3}` for these torus fields, in particular for SIDE24.

**Corollary V2.** For `d ∈ {2, 3}` and every real `L ≥ 24`,

    |(c₃(L) − R_{2/3}(L)) − (J/30 − Ĩ)𝒮_d| ≤ η_{C7}𝒮_d,        η_{C7} = 4.2·10⁻¹⁰⁵ (d = 3),  6.5·10⁻¹⁰⁷ (d = 2).        (V2)

This is at #244 Theorem A's conditional scope. Write `Ĩ = Ĩ_quad + D`, with `Ĩ_quad := −(112/675)Γ(1/6)12^{−1/6}` and `D` as
in (5.3). Then `J/30 − Ĩ ≥ 0.6103 − D`. So `J/30 − Ĩ > 0`, and with it note C7's `ℓ^{2/3}` coefficient at every `L ≥ 24`
(in `d = 2, 3`), as soon as `D ≤ 0.61`.

record.title: asymmetric_elder: An asymmetric fold trap, its attained elder death, and an actual H0 interval summand

statements.text:
For the actual C263 strict-clearance definition

```text
C_M={h: exists y with F(y)>m and a path M->y
                  whose every value is strictly >h},
```

the ridge path proves every h<d belongs to C_M. For h>=d a strict path would cross boundary(D) at a point with height <=d<=h, which is impossible; h>=m is also ruled out by its starting point. Thus

```text
C_M=(-infinity,d),     C_M nonempty,
superlevelBar_deathHeight(F,M)=d<m,
not superlevelBar_isEssential(F,M).                   (5)
```

At active levels M is inside D and P is outside, so `q_alpha j_alpha(1)=1-0=1`. At inactive levels both sides are the identity of the zero vector space. Hence

```text
q j = id_I,
H0({F>=alpha};k) as a persistence module
                   is isomorphic to I direct_sum ker(q). (7)
```

Let Xi_t be the endpoint-candidate process with marks `(ell/t,b,k,A,M/L,u)` as in the frozen higher-configuration proposal. Let Y_t be the process using the actual global H0 elder selector (7), with the **same** endpoint marks and once-counted ordered endpoints. On the Morse/distinct locus Y_t is a subset of Xi_t. For any fixed compact regular mark window W, choose its `Tgap,k_-,a` and constants above. Equations (5), (7) and (12)-(14) show

`Xi_t restricted W = Y_t restricted W` on G_Q.          (15)

record.title: smooth_gaussian_manifold_admission: Admission theorem, actual fold admission for smooth Gaussian fields with dense smooth support

statements.text:
**Admission theorem (subject to the explicit classical imports in Section 12).**
Every law (2) satisfying (1) and the dense-span condition supplies all five
interfaces COUNT, CONTACT, SELECT, ENVELOPE and FAR of ST. In particular the
expected finite ordinary superlevel-H0 elder-bar measure, per volume, has the
canonical finite nonnegative Borel density representative nu defined below,
with

    nu(ell) ~ C_F,g ell^(-1/3),
    E N_bar((0,t]) / V ~ (3/2) C_F,g t^(2/3),                  t -> 0+,    (3)

and 0 < C_F,g < infinity. The essential class is excluded. The coefficient
is the exact local covariance functional (25), or equivalently (27).
The same leading coefficient holds for the ordered maximum/index-(d-1)
candidate-pair density. No selected-density continuity is asserted.

record.title: C3R: Theorem C3-R, Note C3-R, a rate after the ℓ^{2/3} term (Theorem C3 with O(ℓ^{2/3+δ}))

statements.text:
**Theorem C3-R.** In every `d ≥ 2` and for every `L` there are `δ = δ(d) > 0` and `ℓ₀ > 0` such that for `0 < ℓ ≤ ℓ₀`

    ν_cand(ℓ) = cℓ^{−1/3} + B_{d,L} + I^{cand}ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ℓ^{1/3} + c₃ℓ^{2/3} + O(ℓ^{2/3+δ}),                            (C3-R)

with the same `c₃` as (C3). Admissible values: `δ(2) = 1/30`, `δ(3) = 1/50`, `δ(4) = 1/51`, `δ(5) = 1/70`, `δ(6) = 1/89`; in
general `δ(d)` is the value `σ` of Lemma 4 below, and it is positive for every `d`.

**Lemma F₃-R (the fold layer, with error).** Let `0 < α < α_max := 1/2 − mθ/2` for `m ≥ 2` (for `m = 1` no `α` enters).
There are `C, c, N, r₅ > 0` such that for `0 < r ≤ r₅`, `k > 0` and `u`, whenever

    r^{1−2α−mθ} ≤ c k (1 + k)^{−N}     (`m ≥ 2`),        r^{1−θ} ≤ c k (1 + k)^{−N}     (`m = 1`),                         (V)

one has, with `η′ := max(r^{α}, r^{2α/(m−1)})` for `m ≥ 2` and `η′ := r` for `m = 1`,

    |(𝐓_r(k, u) − 𝐒_r(k, u))/r − 𝐋_F(k, u)| ≤ C e^{−ck²}(1 + k)^N [η′(1 + k^{−1}) + r(1 + k^{−2})].                      (F₃-R)

**Lemma T₁-R (the cusp tail, with error).** For `m ≥ 2` let `0 < α′ < α′_max := (1/2)min(1, 2/(m − 1))`; for `m = 1` put
`α′ := 1`. There is `C` such that for `κ ≥ 1` and `u`

    |κ(𝓐(κ, u) − 𝐀₂(0, u)) − a₁(u)| ≤ C κ^{−α′}.                                                                       (T₁-R)

**Lemma 4 (the integration).** Let `m ≥ 2`, `α`, `α′` as above, `a_eff := α` for `m ≤ 3` and `a_eff := 2α/(m − 1)` for
`m ≥ 4`, and `v(α) := (1 − 2α − mθ)/(3(4 − 2α − mθ))`. For every `σ` with `0 < σ ≤ min(v(α), 1/12)`, (C3-R) holds with

    δ = min(σ, a_eff/3 − σ(a_eff + 5), α′/3 − σ(5 + 4α′), 1/3 − 9σ)                                                       (4.0)

whenever this is positive. For `m = 1`, (C3-R) holds with `δ = min(σ, 1/3 − 9σ)` for `0 < σ ≤ min((1 − θ)/(3(4 − θ)), 1/12)`.

record.title: PD: Corollary PD, the planar compact-window rejected-candidate lifetime density with a rate, ν_rej^{B,K}(ℓ) = C_fail^{B,K} ℓ^{2/3} + O(ℓ^{3/4})

statements.text:
**Corollary PD.** There are `ℓ_* ∈ (0, 1]` and `C < ∞`, depending only on `L`, `B` and `K`, such that for `0 < ℓ < ℓ_*` and `0 < t < ℓ_*`:
- **(o) the candidate density:** `|ℓ^{1/3}ν_cand(ℓ) − c_cand| ≤ C ℓ^{1/3}`, that is `ν_cand(ℓ) = c_cand ℓ^{−1/3} + O(1)`. The same holds for `ν_eld`.
- **(i) the rejected density:** `|ν_rej(ℓ) − C_fail ℓ^{2/3}| ≤ C ℓ^{3/4}`.
- **(ii) the cumulative count:** `|E N_rej(0, t] − (3/5)C_fail t^{5/3}| ≤ C t^{7/4}`.
- **(iii) the moments:** for every real `q > −5/3`,

      |E Σ_{nonselected, ℓ ≤ t} ℓ^q − C_fail t^{q+5/3}/(q + 5/3)| ≤ 12C t^{q+7/4}.

- **(iv) the nonselected fraction:** `ν_rej(ℓ)/ν_cand(ℓ) = (C_fail/c_cand)·ℓ + O(ℓ^{13/12})`. Equivalently, `ν_eld(ℓ) = ν_cand(ℓ)[1 − (C_fail/c_cand)ℓ + O(ℓ^{13/12})]`.

record.title: A3_1: QS addendum A3.1, the d ≥ 3 torus lift (Lemma TL_d), the H0 partner (Corollary H_d) and an order-r window certificate (Theorem C_d)

statements.text:
**Statement.** Let `d ≥ 1`, `f ∈ C(X)`, `x₀ ∈ X` and `b := f(x₀)`. Let `Ψ: ℝ^d → ℝ^d` be an invertible affine map, let `ŷ` satisfy `π(Ψ(ŷ)) = x₀`, and let `σ > 0`. Put `g := (f∘π∘Ψ − b)/σ`. Then

    D_f(x₀) = b + σ d_g(ŷ),        with  b + σ(−∞) := −∞.                                                     (TL)

**(E) Elder side.** Suppose `g` satisfies the hypotheses of A3's Theorem QS-E′_d.
- Then `D_f(M_r) = b − kr³ = f(S_r)`, and `M_r` is not a global maximum of `f`.
- If also `f` is Morse with distinct critical values, then the finite ordinary-superlevel H0 class born at `M_r` dies at `S_r` under the elder rule. Its bar is `(b − kr³, b)`.

**(R) Rejected side.** Suppose `g` satisfies the hypotheses of QS-R_d.
- Then `D_f(M_r) > f(S_r)`.
- Suppose also that `f` is Morse with distinct critical values, that `M_r` is a local maximum, and that `S_r` has index `d − 1`. The last two hold on `{W_r > 0}`. Then the class born at `M_r` does not die at `S_r`. That is, the global ordinary elder partner of `M_r` is not `S_r`.

statements.text:
**Lemma 1.1 (C82's density, localized).** Fix `(λ₂, θ, t)` with `λ₂ > 0` and `γ ≠ 0`. For every `U > 0` and every `x > 0`,

    ∫ 1_T 1{λ̃ ≤ U} 1{|μ| ≤ x} w_λ dλ̃ ≤ 192 x U³,                                                              (1.1)

and the left side without the band indicator is at most `12U³`.

**Theorem QFE₃′ (every `β < 1`).** Fix `β ∈ (0, 1)`. There are `C_β < ∞` and `r_β > 0`, uniform over `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ [k₋, k₊]` and the frame, such that for `0 < r ≤ r_β`

    ‖ν_r^F − ν_0^F‖_var ≤ C_βr^β,      1 − p_r = r³α^{(3)} + O_β(r^{3+β}),                                      (4.3)

record.title: A3_4: QS addendum A3.4, the d = 3 soft-layer jet law at rate r under the actual weight (Lemma CM₃, Theorem J₃, Corollary E₃)

statements.text:
**Lemma CM₃.** After reducing `r₀`:
- **(a)** `cI ≤ Cov(V_r) ≤ CI` and `Cov(V_r) − Cov(V₀) = O(r²)`.
- **(b)** Given `U_r = v_r`, `(A, t)` has a Gaussian density `ρ_r` on `Sym(2) × ℝ⁹`, with respect to `dA₁₁ dA₁₂ dA₂₂ dt` (independent entries; Lemma S uses the same coordinates), with `ρ_r(a, t) ≤ Ce^{−c(|a|² + |t|²)}` and

      |ρ_r(a, t) − ρ₀(a, t)| ≤ C r² (1 + |a| + |t|)² e^{−c(|a|² + |t|²)}.                                   (J₃.9′)

- **(c)** For every finite `p ≥ 0` (for `p < 1` by Jensen from `p = 1`),

      E[N^p | U_r = v_r, A = a, t] ≤ C_p (1 + |a| + |t|)^p.                                                 (J₃.10)

**Theorem J₃.** After reducing `r₀`:
- **(J₃.3)** For every finite `q ≥ 0`: `∫_{D_Λ} P^q |g_r − g₀| ≤ C_{Λ,q} r`.
- **(J₃.4)** `0 < m_* ≤ m_Λ ≤ m^* < ∞`, `0 < z_* ≤ z₀ ≤ z^* < ∞`, `|z_r − z₀| ≤ Cr` and `z_r ≥ z_*/2`.
- **(J₃.5)** The normalized law `η_r(E) := r^{−3}Q_r^W((λ̃, λ₂, θ, t) ∈ E)` equals `μ_r/z_r`, with `∫_{D_Λ} P^q |g_r/z_r − g₀/z₀| ≤ Cr`. In particular `Q_r^W(|λ̃| ≤ Λ) = r³m_Λ/z₀ + O(r⁴)`.

**Corollary E₃.** For `i ∈ {M, S}`, finite `p, q ≥ 0` and nonnegative measurable `φ` on `(0, A_*)`:

    r^{−5} E_{Q_r}[W_r N^p P^q 1_{D_Λ∩T} φ(a_i)] ≤ C_{p,q} ∫₀^{A_*} φ(s)(s + r) ds,                          (E₃.2)
    ∫_T P^q φ(a_i) dμ₀ ≤ C_q ∫₀^{A_*} φ(s) s ds.                                                               (E₃.3)

Hence, for `0 < δ ≤ A_*`:

    μ₀(T ∩ {h ≤ δ}) ≤ Cδ²,     r^{−5}E_{Q_r}[W_r N^pP^q 1_{D_Λ∩T}1{h ≤ δ}] ≤ C(δ² + rδ),                  (E₃.4)
    E_{Q_r^W}[N^pP^q 1_{D_Λ∩T}1{h ≤ δ}] ≤ C r³(δ² + rδ),                                                     (E₃.5)
    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ T^c) ≤ C r⁴.                                                                                  (E₃.6)

For every finite `v ≥ 0` and `0 < δ < A_*`:

    r^{−5}E_{Q_r}[W_r N^pP^q 1_{D_Λ∩T} a_i^{−v}1{a_i ≥ δ}] ≤ C ∫_δ^{A_*} [s^{1−v} + r s^{−v}] ds,             (E₃.11)

and `∫_T a_i^{−v} dμ₀` is finite exactly when `v < 2` (E₃.10).

record.title: DC: Lifetime note DC, the stated upper bound D ≤ 0.4389 for the model number D and the sign of note C7's ℓ^{2/3} coefficient at every side L ≥ 10 (the source's heading calls the bound 'certified')

statements.text:
- **Theorem DC** (§7). `D ≤ 0.4389`. More precisely `D ≤ T₁ + T₂ + T₃` (Proposition 1), with
  - `T₁ ≤ 0.0951690`,
  - `T₂ = (28/15)·12^{−7/6}Γ(7/6) ∈ [0.0953758, 0.0953759]`,
  - `T₃ ≤ 0.248277` (Proposition 2),

  so `D ≤ 0.438822`. This holds at #244 Theorem A's conditional scope. Numerically `D ≈ 0.07674` (note V24, Remark 1), so
  the bound is one-sided and far from sharp.

- **Corollary DC1 (the model).** At #244 Theorem A's conditional scope, `Ĩ ≤ −0.17158` and `J/30 − Ĩ ≥ 0.17160`. So in
  `d = 2, 3` the model value `R^∞ = Ĩ𝒮_d` of note SL's coefficient is negative, and the model value `(J/30 − Ĩ)𝒮_d` of note
  C7's coefficient is positive.

- **Corollary DC2 (the torus field).** At #244 Theorem A's conditional scope, for `d ∈ {2, 3}` and every real side `L ≥ 10`
  (SIDE24 included):
  - `(c₃ − R_{2/3})(L) ≥ 0.1711·𝒮_d > 0`;
  - `R_{2/3}(L) ≤ −0.1710·𝒮_d < 0`.

  So, by note C7's (C7.1), for each such `L` the function `ν_eld(ℓ) − cℓ^{−1/3} − c₁ℓ^{1/4} − c₂ℓ^{1/3} − ν_eld^{far,r_0^*}(ℓ)`
  is positive for `0 < ℓ < ℓ₀(d, L)` and of exact order `ℓ^{2/3}`. The threshold `ℓ₀` is not quantified. Note V24's
  Corollary V2 had reduced this sign to `D ≤ 0.61` for `L ≥ 24`. With the `L₀ = 10` columns of its Theorem V, the same
  argument covers every `L ≥ 10` once `D < 0.6099` (in `d = 3`, using `−Ĩ_quad ≥ 0.6104056`). Theorem DC's bound meets
  both conditions.

statements.text:
**Theorem CT.** Fix a>=0, s>0, and an integer p>s. Put theta=1-s/p in (0,1). Under the exact interfaces above,

    E_(P_r)[K^a N^s ; E_r] <= C_(a,s,p) r^3 Pi_r^theta.    (CT)

The same upper bound holds with N_R^s or (N_R)_j, s=j, in place of N^s. In particular, for every fixed delta in (0,1), choosing one fixed integer p>=s/delta and p>s gives

    E_(P_r)[K^a N^s ; E_r] <= C_(a,s,delta) r^3 Pi_r^(1-delta). (CT-delta)

No constant is asserted uniform in p, delta->0, R->infinity, k->0, L or d.
**Proposition NL (abstract obstruction).** The interfaces F and C, even with K=1 and every finite count moment, do not imply E[N^s;E_r]=O(r^3 Pi_r) for any fixed s>0.

record.title: c6_hard_direction_factorization_20260930: Theorem 1 (hard-direction factorization), near cluster coefficients a_j^(d) = R_d(b) a_j^(2)

statements.text:
**Theorem 1 (hard-direction factorization).** For every nonnegative measurable `g` of the soft cubic
coordinates `(s, a, beta, c)`,

    integral g(s, a, beta, c) dM^(d)(s, h, O, tau) = R_d(b) integral g(s, a, beta, c) dM^(2)(s, a, beta, c),   (1)

with

    R_d(b) = N_d(b) m_(2,b) / m_(d,b),                                                                     (2)
    N_d(b) = c_m (2 pi)^(-m(m-1)/4) integral_(0 < h_2 < ... < h_m) prod_j h_j^3 phi_2(h_j - b) prod_(i<j) (h_j - h_i) dh,
    m_(d,b) = E[(det A)^2 1{A negative definite}],   A = -b I_m + G_m,
    m_(2,b) = E[A^2 1{A < 0}],                        A ~ N(-b, 2),

where `phi_2` is the `N(0, 2)` density and `G_m` is the `m x m` GOE matrix with independent `N(0, 2)` diagonal and
`N(0, 1)` off-diagonal entries (`N_2 = 1`, `m_(2,b)` is Math-#168's `m_(2,b)`, `R_2 = 1`). The factor `R_d(b)` does
not depend on `k`.

**Corollary 1 (near coefficients).** The [SC] (20) coefficients satisfy `a_j^(d)(b, k) = R_d(b) a_j^(2)(b, k)`,
`j = 1, 2`. Hence `a_2 / a_1` (the near doublet-to-singleton ratio, `nu_near(2)/nu_near(1)`), and every law
obtained by normalizing a function of `(s, a, beta, c)` under `dM` by a positive finite mass (`0 < integral g dM
< infinity`; the factor `R_d(b)` is positive and finite and cancels) — the conditional law of the soft cubic given
`n >= 1`, the shape region measure `Q du dv` of [R] (R9)–(R10), the Pareto-11 radius law and the constants
`E eta = 5771/7062`, `I, J, D, E0` and all ratios of [R], [E], [Q], [ELD] — are the same in every dimension
`d >= 2`, for the continuum-kernel measures `dM^(d)`. The radial-tail constant of [R] (R13) satisfies `C_*^(d) = R_d(b) C_*^(2)`, since (R12)'s `J_cusp`
integrand has the same hard-direction factor (section 3).

**Corollary 2 (conditional, elder statements).** Where a source identifies `lim r^(-3) (1 - p_r) = a_1 + a_2`
(#170 Theorem S in `d = 2`, #175 Theorem F in `d >= 3`, both unmerged drafts), the elder-failure coefficient in
dimension `d` is `R_d(b) (alpha_1 + alpha_2)^(2)`, and the conditional lifetime-fraction and shape laws given
failure (#170 section 8.8, #175 M1, #179/#181's `S \ O2` laws) are dimension-independent. This corollary inherits
those sources' conditional status and promotes nothing. It concerns the sources' statements read for the same
continuum-kernel model as Theorem 1; the sources are stated for the periodized field on `T_L^d`, and a finite-`L`
theorem does not transfer to the continuum measures by replacing its covariance in notation, so no new
actual-field theorem is claimed here.

statements.text:
**Theorem P (the candidate density with remainder `ℓ^{3/5}`).** For every `d ≥ 2` and `L > 0`, as `ℓ ↓ 0`,

    ν_cand(ℓ) = c ℓ^{−1/3} + B_{d,L} + I^{cand} ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ ℓ^{1/3} + O(ℓ^{3/5}).                                (P.1)

**Lemma U.** There are `C, r₃ > 0` such that for `0 < r ≤ r₃`, `k ≥ r²` (that is, `κ ≥ r`) and `u ∈ S^{d−1}`,

    |𝐓_r(k, u) − r^{−2}𝐀_0(k, u) − [𝐀₂(k, u) − 𝐀₂(0, u)] − 𝓐(k/r, u)| ≤ C(r² + r min(k, 1/k)).                  (U.1)

statements.text:
**The sign of `B₂`** is that of `𝒬`, and (checker C5)

    𝒬 = 4λ₂²(λ₄λ₈ − λ₆²) + D(25λ₄² − λ₂λ₆) = 4λ₂²λ₄σ₄² + D(24λ₄² − D),

so `B₂ > 0` whenever `λ₂λ₆ ≤ 25λ₄²` (the Gaussian kernel has `λ₂λ₆/λ₄² = 5/3`, the mixture of §6.2 `1625/867`). The sign
is not fixed by (H) (Codex, review of v1 on #214): for `L = 2π` and the spectrum with weights `1 − 10⁻⁵` and `10⁻⁵` at the
frequencies `1` and `40`, `λ₂λ₆/λ₄² ≈ 58.8` and `𝒬 ≈ −7.09·10⁸ < 0`; adding small positive, rapidly decaying weights at
every other frequency gives (H) and, `𝒬` being continuous in `(λ₂, λ₄, λ₆, λ₈)`, keeps `𝒬 < 0`.

statements.text:
**Lemma S‴ (the elder weight on `κ ≤ r`).** There are `r_* > 0` and `C, N` such that for `0 < r ≤ r_*`, `b ∈ R`,
`u ∈ S^{d−1}` and `0 < k ≤ r²`,

    E_Q[(W_r/r²) e] ≤ C r² [ rκ + r^{7/3}κ^{2/3}log(2/r) + min(r^{7/2}, r^{3/2}κ^{2/3}) ] P^N,                          (S‴.1)
    0 ≤ 𝐓_r^{eld}(k, u) ≤ C [ rκ + r^{7/3}κ^{2/3}log(2/r) + min(r^{7/2}, r^{3/2}κ^{2/3}) ].                              (S‴.2)

**Corollary EM (the elder and rejected densities).** As `ℓ ↓ 0`,

    ν_eld(ℓ) = c ℓ^{−1/3} + c₁ ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ ℓ^{1/3} + O(ℓ^{9/14}),                                                      (EM.1)
    ρ_rej(ℓ) = B_{d,L} + (I^{cand} − c₁) ℓ^{1/4} + O(ℓ^{3/5}).                                                          (EM.2)

record.title: full_spectrum_enclosure_method_20261018: interval-enclosure METHOD for C_alg(d,L), cone-weight Lemma (M20) and conditional regression bound (M30)

statements.text: Call the right side of the original equation (1) C_alg(d,L). The result of this unit is a finite, in-principle terminating interval-enclosure METHOD for C_alg at the ORIGINAL fixed finite d>=2 and L>0, once d is given and L is supplied as a computable positive real with certified interval access. It uses the full original spectrum, with analytically bounded omitted sums. It does not replace the covariance by a cutoff field, replace L by infinity, remove the zero mode, or change height conditioning.

**Lemma.** For real symmetric n by n matrices A,B with operator norms at most R,

\[
|w(A)-w(B)|\le 2n R^{2n-1}\|A-B\|_{\rm op},\qquad n\ge1.\tag{M20}
\]

A concrete certificate-producing scheme is therefore:

1. Obtain certified intervals for the ACTUAL fixed positive L, pi and the finite sums in M14 at positive integer cutoff M, with outward tails M15. Enclose a,b,c; compute strict floors from M12–M13 and the bounds in Section 3. If an interval floor remains nonpositive, refine it or use the positive witness bounds. Do not infer positivity from a floating midpoint.
2. For a requested absolute coefficient tolerance epsilon>0, choose a POSITIVE INTEGER Gaussian radius R with the certified upper bound in M27 <=epsilon/3. This is possible because that bound tends to zero along the positive integers; no sample/model computation is needed.
3. With the positive integer R from Step 2, partition each compact (x,z) rectangle into finitely many boxes with rational endpoints and hence exact rational volumes. On each box enclose e,U,B,Gamma,L_e,V,J and phi_N by outward interval operations. Use M21 with a rational matrix center to enclose w, then multiply the nonnegative factor intervals. Sum each interval times its exact rational box volume, and sum faces. Let the resulting truncated-integral interval be [ell_R,u_R]. All moment and elementary-function uncertainties remain inside this interval.
4. Refine the moment/input/constant intervals and box partitions until u_R-ell_R<=2epsilon/3. Output [ell_R,u_R+E_G^upper(R)]. The true C_alg lies in this interval, whose width is <=epsilon.

One precise limited implication is available. Let X be the actual centered Gaussian field as a random element of its physical Sobolev Hilbert space H^k, with M_k=E||X||_(H^k)^2<infinity. Let Y be a finite centered Gaussian pin vector with covariance Sigma>=lambda I>0. Gaussian Hilbert-space regression yields

\[
E[\|X\|_{H^k}^2\mid Y=y]
 \le M_k(1+|y|^2/\lambda).\tag{M30}
\]

statements.text:
**Theorem SE″_K (the sector errors by shells).** Under the standing conditions and `r ≤ min(r₁, r₂)`, with `C_VH²r^{1/4} ≤ 1`, define

    Good^{E″} := ⋃_{j=0}^{J}(S_j^E ∩ Good_sel(r, w_j)),      Good^{R″} := ⋃_{j=0}^{J}(S_j^R ∩ Good_LE,K(r, w_j)),

where `Good_sel(r, w) := E ∩ {Rbox ≤ w, E0(r, w) < min(v, −μ)/2, H_M^{err}(r, w) < 1, H_S^{err}(r, w) < 2/5}` is C103 §4's selected good event and `Good_LE,K(r, w)` is A4.1's Corollary LE_K event. Then `D_f(M_r) = f(S_r)` on `Good^{E″}` and `D_f(M_r) > f(S_r)` on `Good^{R″}` (so, on the Morse locus, `H_r` holds on the first and fails on the second), and

    μ_r(E ∖ Good^{E″}) ≤ C_K[r^{3/2} + r^{7/4}H³ + H⁵r^{5/4} + H⁷r^{13/8} + rH⁴ + H²r log(1/r) + r^{3/2}H⁴log(1/r) + H⁵r^{3/2}],   (3.1)
    μ_r(Rsec ∖ Good^{R″}) ≤ C_K[r^{3/2} + r^{7/4}H³ + rH⁴ + H³r + r^{3/2}H⁴ + r²H³log(1/r)].                                  (3.2)

**Theorem SE″_K, continued (the fixed layer).** For fixed `Λ ≥ 1`, uniformly over `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ K` and frames, for `0 < r ≤ r_{K,Λ}`,

    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ (H_r Δ E)) ≤ C_{K,Λ}r⁴log(1/r),                                                                (3.3)

and C103 (S28)'s two comparisons hold with `C_{K,Λ}r log(1/r)` in place of `C·Rerr`.

**Theorem QFE″_K (every `β < 1`).** Fix `β ∈ (0, 1)`. There are `C_{K,β} < ∞` and `r_{K,β} > 0`, uniform over `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ K` and frames, such that for `0 < r ≤ r_{K,β}`

    ‖ν_r^F − ν_0^F‖_var ≤ C_{K,β}r^β,      1 − p_r = r³(α₁ + α₂) + O_{K,β}(r^{3+β}),                                 (4.3)

and the raw-jet law conditional on failure converges at the same rate.

**Theorem ER′_K (the endpoint).** There are `C_K < ∞` and `r_K ∈ (0, e^{−1}]`, uniform over `b ∈ B₀`, `k ∈ K` and frames, such that for `0 < r < r_K`

    ‖ν_r^F − ν_0^F‖_var ≤ C_Kr log(1/r)⁴,      1 − p_r = r³(α₁ + α₂) + O_K(r⁴log(1/r)⁴),                              (4.4)

and the raw-jet law conditional on failure converges at the same rate.

statements.text:
**Corollary PD₃.** There are `ℓ_* ∈ (0, e^{−1}]` and `C < ∞`, depending only on `L`, `B` and `K`, such that for `0 < ℓ, t < ℓ_*`:
- **(o) the candidate density:** `|ℓ^{1/3}ν_cand(ℓ) − c_cand| ≤ Cℓ^{1/3}`, that is `ν_cand(ℓ) = c_candℓ^{−1/3} + O(1)`; the same holds for `ν_eld`.
- **(i) the rejected density:** `|ν_rej(ℓ) − C_fail^{(3)}ℓ^{2/3}| ≤ Cℓ^{8/9}log(1/ℓ)^{8/3}`.
- **(ii) the cumulative count:** `|EN_rej(0, t] − (3/5)C_fail^{(3)}t^{5/3}| ≤ 3Ct^{17/9}log(1/t)^{8/3}`.
- **(iii) the moments:** for every real `q > −5/3`, `|EΣ_{nonselected, ℓ ≤ t}ℓ^q − C_fail^{(3)}t^{q+5/3}/(q + 5/3)| ≤ 3073Ct^{q+17/9}log(1/t)^{8/3}`.
- **(iv) the nonselected fraction:** `ν_rej(ℓ)/ν_cand(ℓ) = (C_fail^{(3)}/c_cand)ℓ + O(ℓ^{11/9}log(1/ℓ)^{8/3})`; equivalently `ν_eld(ℓ) = ν_cand(ℓ)[1 − (C_fail^{(3)}/c_cand)ℓ + O(ℓ^{11/9}log(1/ℓ)^{8/3})]`.
- **(v) the power-law family:** for each fixed `β ∈ (0, 2/3)` there are `ℓ_β` and `C_β` such that (i)–(iv) hold for `ℓ, t < ℓ_β` with `C_βℓ^{(2+β)/3}`, `C_βt^{(5+β)/3}`, `C_βt^{q+(5+β)/3}` and `C_βℓ^{1+β/3}` in place of the logarithmic errors. The density exponent's supremum `8/9` is attained in (i) up to the logarithm.

statements.text:
**Proposition D₃.** Let `0 < r ≤ 1` and `w ≥ 1` with `r^{1/2}w ≤ 1`. Put `Ω := Ω_w`, `ε := 4√(k/λ₂)` and `ξ := kN/λ₂`, and set

    C_B := max(16, 2A₂, (c₀ + A₁)²),    C_e := (c₀ + A₁)²,    D_h := 2(K₂ + A₄),
    c₃ := c₁ + 1 + 1/k₋ + A₃,    C_h := 2c₂(c₀ + A₁) + 2c₃².

At `k₋ = k₊ = 1`: `C_B = 16`, `C_e = 28561/2304`, `D_h = 259/24` and `C_h = 134377/288`. Suppose

    λ₂ > C_B k N² r w⁴.                                                                                        (B_r)

Then:
- **(a) The barrel.** `r^{1/2}ε < w`. On `Ω × [−ε, ε]`, `g := 𝔉` satisfies (B1)–(B3) with `Λ_b := λ₂/k − A₂Nrw > λ₂/(2k)`. So A3's Lemma SR applies, and the reduced height `G(X, ζ) := max_{|η|≤ε} 𝔉(X, ζ, η)` is defined and `C²` on `Ω`.
- **(b) The bounds.** In raw coordinates, with operator norms,

      sup_Ω |G − G_k| ≤ N r w⁴ (K₀ + C_e ξ),        sup_Ω ‖D²(G − G_k)‖ ≤ N r w² (D_h + C_h ξ).                (D₃)

  No factor `1/γ` appears.

**Theorem G₃.** Fix budgets `τ₀, τ_M, τ_S > 0`. For `0 < r ≤ r₀` and a deterministic `w ≥ 1` with `r^{1/2}w ≤ 1`, define inside `D_Λ`

    G₃(r, w) := T ∩ {γ ≠ 0} ∩ (B_r) ∩ {sup_Ω |G − G_k| < τ₀} ∩ {H_M < τ_M} ∩ {H_S < τ_S}.                      (G₃.1)

On `(B_r)`, `G` and `H_i` are those of Proposition D₃ and Lemma T₃. Put `λ_* := C_λ k r w⁴`, with `C_λ := max(C_B, 2C_e/τ₀)`, and `σ_i := rw²/τ_i`. Then for every finite `p ≥ 1`:

    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ T ∩ {γ ≠ 0} ∩ (B_r) ∩ {H_i ≥ τ_i}) ≤ C r³(σ_i² + rσ_i) ≤ C r⁵w⁴,                                   (G₃.2)
    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ T ∩ {λ₂ ≤ δ_λN²}) ≤ C r³(δ_λ⁴ + rδ_λ²) for every δ_λ > 0;  at δ_λ = λ_*: ≤ C(r⁷w^{16} + r⁶w⁸),    (G₃.3)
    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∩ {2K₀Nrw⁴ ≥ τ₀}) ≤ C_p r³(2K₀rw⁴/τ₀)^p,                                                            (G₃.4)
    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∖ G₃) ≤ C_p[r⁴ + r⁵w⁴ + r⁶w⁸ + r⁷w^{16} + r³(rw⁴)^p].                                                (G₃.5)

`G₃` does not depend on `p`; in (G₃.5) `p` is free. In particular, let `w = r^{−β}` with `0 ≤ β ≤ 3/16`, and choose `p ≥ 1/(1 − 4β)` in (G₃.5). Then

    Q_r^W(D_Λ ∖ G₃) ≤ C r⁴,    Q_r^W(G₃) = r³m_Λ/z₀ + O(r⁴),    Q_r^W(G₃ | D_Λ) = 1 − O(r).                      (G₃.6)

For `3/16 < β < 1/4`, choose `p ≥ 4`. Then the term `r⁷w^{16}` is the largest, tied with the value term at `p = 4`, and `Q_r^W(G₃ | D_Λ) = 1 − O(r^{4−16β})`. All constants may depend on the budgets and `p`.

record.title: TL: Theorem TL (the rejected kernel on the soft layer) and Corollaries TL1–TL3 (elder density with remainder ℓ^{4/9}log(1/ℓ))

statements.text:
**Theorem TL (the rejected kernel on the soft layer).** There are `r₀ > 0` and `C` such that for `0 < r ≤ r₀`, `κ ≥ 1` with
`k = κr ≤ 1`, and `u ∈ S^{d−1}`,

    |𝐓_r^{rej}(k, u) − 𝓐^{rej}(κ, u)| ≤ C r² (1 + κ).                                                                  (TL)

**Corollary TL1 (the separations with `ℓ/r⁴ ≥ 1`).** As `ℓ ↓ 0`,

    ∫_0^{ℓ^{1/4}}∫_{S^{d−1}} 𝐓_r^{rej}(ℓ/r³, u) dσ(u) dr = ℓ^{1/4}∫_0^1∫_{S^{d−1}} 𝓐^{rej}(s^{−4}, u) dσ(u) ds + O(ℓ^{2/3}).   (TL1)

**Corollary TL2 (the moving band of Math-#296).** With #296's `J_ℓ(y) = k_ℓB_{r_ℓ}(k_ℓ)/r_ℓ³`,
`r_ℓ = ℓ^{3/10}y^{−1/10}`, `k_ℓ = ℓ^{1/10}y^{3/10}` and `B_r(k) = ∫∫A_r^{rej} db dσ`, and with `F̄₀ := ∫∫F₀ db dσ`
(#242 (1.0)): for every `0 < y₁ < y₂ < ∞` there is `C` with `|J_ℓ(y) − F̄₀| ≤ Cℓ^{1/5}` for `y ∈ [y₁, y₂]` and small `ℓ`.
Hence #296's band contribution (its `ν_{[a,b]}` with `[a, b] = [y₁, y₂]`) is
`(ℓ^{1/2}/10)F̄₀∫_{y₁}^{y₂}y^{−3/2} dy + O(ℓ^{7/10})`.

**Corollary TL3 (the elder and rejected densities).** As `ℓ ↓ 0`,

    ν_eld(ℓ) = c ℓ^{−1/3} + c₁ ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ ℓ^{1/3} + ν_eld^{far,r_0^*}(ℓ) + O(ℓ^{4/9} log(1/ℓ)),                      (TL3.1)

    E_{Q^W}[K^a ; N_R>0, h_{q+1}<=eta]

record.title: far_elder_flat_ridge_20260930: Theorem G (living bars have flat components; the far elder density is O(ℓ^N) for every N)

statements.text:
**Theorem G.** For every `ρ ∈ (0, L/4]` and every integer `N ≥ 1` there is `C = C(d, L, ρ, N) < ∞` such that

    ν_eld^{far,ρ}(ℓ) ≤ C ℓ^N,        0 < ℓ ≤ 1.                                                    (0.2)

Consequently, for `0 < t ≤ 1`, `E N_eld^{far,ρ}(0, t] ≤ C t^{N+1}/(N+1)` per unit volume, and for every real `q`
(however negative) `E Σ_{far elder bars, ℓ_i ≤ t} ℓ_i^q < ∞`: the far elder population has all inverse-lifetime
moments.

**Lemma 1 (flat components).** Let `f ∈ C²(X)` and `K > 0` with `K ≥ sup_X ‖D²f‖_op`. Let `x_0` be a local maximum,
`b = f(x_0)`, and let `t < b` be such that the connected component `C_t` of `x_0` in the open set `{f > t}`
contains no point with `f > b`. Then for every `p ∈ C_t`

    |∇f(p)|² ≤ 2K (b − f(p)) ≤ 2K (b − t).                                                          (1.1)

The hypothesis holds exactly for `t ≥ b − ℓ(x_0)`, where `ℓ(x_0)` is the lifetime of the `H_0` bar of `x_0` under
the superlevel filtration with the elder rule ([P] §8): as long as the bar is alive, its component contains no
older (higher) maximum, and a component with a point above `b` would contain one (§1).

**Lemma 2 (crossing).** If the death partner `y` of `x_0` satisfies `dist(x_0, y) ≥ ρ`, then for `t = b − ℓ(x_0)`
the component `C_t` meets every sphere `∂B(x_0, r)`, `0 < r < ρ`, and on `C_t` one has `b − ℓ(x_0) < f ≤ b` and
`|∇f| < (2Kℓ(x_0))^{1/2}`.

**Lemma 3 (near-critical balls).** If `|∇f(p)| ≤ (2K_0ℓ)^{1/2}`, `b − ℓ < f(p) ≤ b`, `sup‖D²f‖ ≤ K_0` and
`r_ℓ = (ℓ/K_0)^{1/2}`, then every `q ∈ B(p, r_ℓ)` satisfies `|∇f(q)| ≤ 3(K_0ℓ)^{1/2}` and `|f(q) − b| ≤ 3ℓ`.

- (c) *Consequence for the constant in (0.2).* Suppose (b)'s (2.4) holds for the density (0.1). Then for every `N ≥ 1`
     there are `c_N > 0` and `ρ_N > 0` such that every constant admissible in (0.2) satisfies

         C(d, L, ρ, N) ≥ c_N ρ^{1−4N},      0 < ρ ≤ ρ_N.                                                  (R6.1)

record.title: finite_l_d2_coefficient_20261018: rational enclosure of the original finite-L d2 collision expression C_alg(2,24)

statements.text:
This package evaluates only the explicit original collision expression
C_alg(2,24), with physical derivatives, the complete infinite lattice
spectrum and the common full normalizer including the zero mode. It does
not evaluate a cutoff field, remove the spatial mean, condition on common
height or add a volume or pair-count factor. The original source hash is
f38c085ab5b15368e6989a1fd6298490f3b671f5a6c3a01bcdc81b516022bc33.

Let a=mu2, b=mu4, c=mu6. With t=e1^2 e2^2 in [0,1/4], the d2 precheck gives
D(t)=a^2*b+(b-3a^2)(b+a^2)t and
V(t)=c-b^2/a+3(b^2/a+3ab-3a^3-c)t. The conditional transverse Gaussian
has variance a^2(b^2-a^4)/D(t); its squared negative half-axis moment is
half that variance. The original full sphere is the full physical angle
of area2pi, not an average or hemisphere.

The exact reduction before bounding is

    C_alg = Gamma(7/6)*a*(b^2-a^4)
            /(8*24^(1/3)*pi^(5/2))
            * integral_0^(2pi) V(t(theta))^(2/3)/D(t(theta))^(3/2) dtheta.

For every angle, independent positive D and V hulls bound the ratio by
V_lo^(2/3)/D_hi^(3/2) and V_hi^(2/3)/D_lo^(3/2). Integrating multiplies
by the full2pi. H=beta*(b+a^2)=b^2-a^4 is positive. Thus positive interval
endpoints can be raised to the sixth power using

    C_bound^6 = Gamma^6*a^6*H^6*V_bound^4
                /(4^6*24^2*pi^9*D_bound^9).

Use all lower positive numerator endpoints and upper denominator endpoints
for the lower bound, and conversely for the upper bound. This bounds the
whole angular integral; it is not a claim that the angular integrand is
constant. The final unit is physical length^-2 as in the original M1.

statements.text:
Here is the new assertion. There exist a nonempty compact rectangular
parameter box U around (6,22,24), with coordinates (alpha,beta,q), a finite
R>0, and r_0>0, such that the actual ordinary finite superlevel-H0 elder
bars whose birth maxima satisfy the Borel sector mark in Section 2 have
expected lifetime measure per area

    M_A4(B)=V^-1 E N_A4(B),   B subset (0,infinity) Borel.

On a fixed interval (0,ell_0), this measure has the particular finite Borel
density given by (26), and

    nu_A4(ell) ~ C_A4 ell^(4/5),
    M_A4((0,t]) ~ (5/9) C_A4 t^(9/5),       ell,t -> 0+,              (3)

where 0<C_A4<infinity and the explicit contact coefficient is (28).
Every counted maximum dies at the farther of its two nearby saddles in the
selected direction, despite a nearer intervening saddle. The identification
is the genuine global elder death on X. It is not nearest-saddle pairing.

Thus the coefficient in (3) is exactly

    C_A4=(36/(5V)) integral_{X,S^1,K}
        alpha a^2 L_0(alpha,beta,q)^(-9/5)
        p_{x,u}(z_0(b,a,zeta,q)) h(x,u)
                                     dK dtheta dx.                (28)

In fact they give the law/sector-dependent estimate

    nu_A4(ell)=C_A4 ell^(4/5)+O(ell),       ell ->0+,                (29)

record.title: C3: Theorem C3, the ℓ^{2/3} term of the candidate density, with Lemmas F₃ and T₁, Propositions G and G″ and Corollary G′

statements.text:
**Lemma F₃ (the fold layer at order `r`).** For every `k > 0` and `u`,

    lim_{r↓0} (𝐓_r(k, u) − 𝐒_r(k, u))/r = 𝐋_F(k, u).                                                              (F₃)

**Lemma T₁ (the cusp tail).** For every `u`, `lim_{κ→∞} κ(𝓐(κ, u) − 𝐀₂(0, u)) = a₁(u)`. Moreover `a₁(u) = (1/10)∫_RF₀(b, u)db`,
with `F₀` as in #242 (1.0).

**Theorem C3 (the `ℓ^{2/3}` term of the candidate density).** In every `d ≥ 2` and for every `L`, `|𝐄(k, u)| ≤ C min(k, 1/k)`
for `k > 0`, and as `ℓ ↓ 0`

    ν_cand(ℓ) = c ℓ^{−1/3} + B_{d,L} + I^{cand} ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ ℓ^{1/3} + c₃ ℓ^{2/3} + o(ℓ^{2/3}),
    c₃ := (1/3) ∫_{S^{d−1}} ∫_0^∞ 𝐄(k, u) k^{−5/3} dk dσ(u).                                                       (C3)

**Proposition G (the Gaussian kernel).** Let `C(z) = e^{−|z|²/2}` on `R^d` (the model case of #242 §0), `d ≥ 2`, and
evaluate (0.3) and (C3) on the model's jet law. Then:
- (G.1) For every `k` and every unit `e ⊥ u`, under `Q̄_{0,k}` the pair `(γ_e, B_ee)` is independent of `A`, and its law is that
  of two independent `N(0, 2)` variables, not depending on `k`. Moreover `p_{V_0}(v(k)) = e^{−12k²}p_{V_0}(v(0))`.

statements.text:
**Lemma SL₀ (the fold limit after birth integration).** For every `k > 0` and `u ∈ S^{d−1}`,
`lim_{r↓0} κ𝐓_r^{rej}(k, u) = ℱ(k, u)`, with `κ = k/r`. Moreover `0 ≤ ℱ(k, u) ≤ Ce^{−ck²}(1 + k)^N` for all `k > 0`, and
`0 ≤ ℱ₀(u) ≤ C`.

**Corollary SL₁ (the matching).** For `0 < k ≤ 1` and `u ∈ S^{d−1}`,

    |ℱ(k, u) − ℱ₀(u)| ≤ C k².                                                                                         (SL₁)

**Theorem SL (the soft layer to `o(ℓ^{2/3})`).** In every `d ≥ 2` and for every `L`, as `ℓ ↓ 0`,

    ∫_0^{ℓ^{1/4}}∫_{S^{d−1}} 𝐓_r^{rej}(ℓ/r³, u) dσ(u) dr = ℓ^{1/4}∫_0^1∫_{S^{d−1}} 𝓐^{rej}(s^{−4}, u) dσ(u) ds + R_{2/3} ℓ^{2/3} + o(ℓ^{2/3}),
    R_{2/3} := ∫_{S^{d−1}}∫_0^∞ v⁴ (ℱ(v^{−3}, u) − ℱ₀(u)) dv dσ(u).                                                     (SL)

The integrand of `R_{2/3}` is bounded by `C min(1, v^{−2})`, so the integral converges absolutely.

record.title: small_lifetime_shape_20260930: small-lifetime doublets, exact shape limit (Theorem 1) and singular companion-moment crossover (Theorems 2-4)

statements.text:
**Lemma 1.** Let c(e)>0 be the unique root of

                  2c^3+3e c^2=e^2.                     (3)

On the support of (1), n=1 exactly for x<=c(e), and n=2 exactly for x>c(e),
up to tie null sets. In particular 0<c(e)<b(e) for 0<e<1. It would be false
to assert that every sufficiently short, but nonzero, e already forces a doublet.

**Theorem 1 (shape and multiplicity).** The law of (Y,W) converges in total
variation at O(sqrt(epsilon)) to independent variables with densities

 f_Y(y)=4y^3, 0<y<1,
 f_W(w)=(81/13)w(1-w^4), 0<w<1/sqrt(3).                 (7)

The singleton probability has the more singular expansion

 Pi_epsilon(n=1)=C_s epsilon^(1/3)+O(epsilon^(2/3)),
                   C_s=(486/169)2^(-2/3)>0.             (8)

Consequently doublets tend to probability one. For the TAGGED joint law,

 dTV(Law_Pi_epsilon(n,Y,W), delta_2 x Law(Y,W in (7)))
             =C_s epsilon^(1/3)+O(epsilon^(1/2)).        (9)

No rate is asserted for physical marks obtained through epsilon-dependent
singular maps; their convergence below is weak.

**Theorem 2.** Under Pi_epsilon, the companion ratio, defined on doublets,
converges in distribution to

                 V0=(1-W^2)/(2W^2)>1.                  (14)

It is independent of Y in (7). Its exact density and survival function are

 g(v)=(81/13)[(2v+1)^(-2)-(2v+1)^(-4)], v>1,
 P(V0>t)=81/[26(2t+1)]-27/[26(2t+1)^3], t>=1.            (15)

In particular P(V0>t)~(81/52)t^-1. Its nonnegative moments are finite exactly
below 1; E[min(V0,T)]~(81/52)log T. The reciprocal rho0 has density

                 (324/13)(1+rho)/(2+rho)^4, 0<rho<1.    (16)

The other saddle's downward height e_c satisfies, jointly,

 (e/epsilon, e_c/e, e_c/epsilon)
                  -> (Y, H(V0), Y H(V0)),
 H(v)=v^3(v+2)/(2v+1).                                 (17)

This convergence is weak, including sentinel removal using (8).

**Theorem 3 (a uniform tail envelope in the algebraic law).** For sufficiently
small epsilon and all T>=1,

 Pi_epsilon,2(V>T)
       <= C min(T^-1, epsilon^-4 T^-13).                 (23)

For each FIXED epsilon>0,

 Pi_epsilon,2(V>T)
       ~ [165888 H0/(13 B_epsilon)] T^-13,
                         H0=6401/3960.                 (24)

Hence its nonnegative moments are finite exactly for p<13 at every positive
epsilon. The exponent1 emerges only after epsilon->0. There is no
contradiction or unmentioned transfer of uniform integrability.

**Theorem 4.** Under Pi_epsilon,2, as epsilon->0:

 0<=p<1: E[V^p] -> E[V0^p]<infinity;
 p=1:    E[V] = (27/52) log(1/epsilon)+O(1);
 1<p<13: E[V^p] ~ K_p epsilon^(-(p-1)/3),
 p>=13:  E[V^p]=infinity for every fixed epsilon>0,       (25)

where the positive finite coefficient is explicitly

 K_p=2592/[13(13-p)] * 2^(-(13-p)/3)
        * integral_0^1 z^((2p-5)/3)(1+z)^((p-1)/3) dz.   (26)

For example K_4=30/13, K_7=441/65, and K_10=3270/91.
The normalization may instead be Pi_epsilon with the moment restricted to n=2;
its leading asymptotics agree because Pi_epsilon(n=2)->1. No statement is made
about these moments in the original finite-r field.

    E_Q[(W_r/r²) e] ≤ C r² (κ + r) κ^{2/3} P^N,                                                                     (S″.1)
    0 ≤ r^{−2}A_r^{eld}(b, k, u) ≤ C (κ + r) κ^{2/3} (1 + |b|)^N e^{−cb²},        0 ≤ 𝐓_r^{eld}(k, u) ≤ C (κ + r) κ^{2/3}.   (S″.2)

`0 < r ≤ r₀`, `r^θ ≤ κ ≤ 1` and `u ∈ S^{d−1}`,

    |𝐓_r^{rej}(k, u) − 𝓐^{rej}(κ, u)| ≤ C (κr² + r³/κ).                                                              (TL⁻)

**Corollary TS (the elder and rejected densities).** As `ℓ ↓ 0`,

    ν_eld(ℓ) = c ℓ^{−1/3} + c₁ ℓ^{1/4} + c₂ ℓ^{1/3} + ν_eld^{far,r_0^*}(ℓ) + O(ℓ^{4/7} log(1/ℓ)),                       (TS.1)

record.title: cap_i4_d3_spectral_adapter_20261005: Cap I4 in d=3, explicit 2x2 spectral pushforward domination (S2) and ninth-moment depth envelope (10)

statements.text:
Suppose the law of B has entry-coordinate density p satisfying

    p(B) <= C0 exp(-c||B||_F^2),  C0>=0, c>0.             (4)

No invariance is assumed for p. The majorant is radial in Frobenius coordinates. By (3),

    q_+(lambda,Lambda)
      <= pi C0 (Lambda-lambda) exp(-c(lambda^2+Lambda^2))
                           1_{0<lambda<Lambda}.           (5)

Equivalently, with `e(B)=(lambda,Lambda)`,

    e_*(Law(B) restricted to {B>0}) <= sigma_2,
    sigma_2 = pi C0 (Lambda-lambda) exp(-c(lambda^2+Lambda^2))
                         1_{0<lambda<Lambda} d lambda d Lambda. (S2)

Consequently a fully displayed sufficient constant is

    C_depth = 256 pi C0 A B_* [M9 sqrt(pi)/(4c^(3/2)) + 60/c^6],
    E_Q[W 1_E_lambda] <= C_depth r^5.                      (10)

Assume the actual FULL normalizer `Z=E_Q W>=cZ r^2`, cZ>0. Divide (10) exactly once:

    Q^W(E_lambda) <= (C_depth/cZ)r^3.                      (11)

A raw unweighted fourth moment alone is not (12)'s premise. The cap-failure union and the implication on W>0 supplied by the deterministic source therefore give

    Q^W(G^c) <= (C_depth/cZ)r^3
                + M4joint/[cZ(3k_floor/10)^4]r^4.          (13)
